minor.issue: Filters by role='user'; if the current user's primary account has role 'super_admin' or 'sub_admin', primary is EXCLUDED from positions list. Only affects admin accounts using re-entry, not regular users. Recommend removing the role filter or including current user's role.

ui_bugs.issue: TOTAL_POTENTIAL constant (203,699,600 = ₹20,36,99,600) shown on /business-plan and /compensation-plan does NOT match the sum of INCOME_LEVELS[].total which is 192,099,600 (₹19,20,99,600). Calculator computes 6^n × per_level correctly and yields ₹19,20,99,600 — proving the constant / per-level table is inconsistent. Either one of the per-level `per` values is wrong (compare against real infographic) OR TOTAL_POTENTIAL should be 192,099,600. Reverse-mode also affected: target=₹1,00,00,000 returns directs=5 (correct math for current rates) but review request expected 6.

action_items: Reconcile TOTAL_POTENTIAL vs INCOME_LEVELS in /app/frontend/src/lib/plan-theme.js. Compute: sum(per*6^L for L=1..8 with per=[1200,400,50,300,50,200,50,100]) = 192,099,600 (₹19,20,99,600) — NOT 203,699,600. Confirm against source infographic and fix either the per-level rates OR the TOTAL_POTENTIAL constant so /business-plan, /compensation-plan, Landing, and Calculator all agree.
OPTIONAL: /api/mlm/my-positions currently filters by role='user'; consider removing role filter so admin accounts that create re-entry positions still see their primary in the list.

Firebase Web SDK config in /app/frontend/.env produced 'auth/invalid-api-key' at runtime (not the expected 'auth/unauthorized-domain'). The graceful fallback to /auth/otp/send + dev-OTP box works correctly, so functionally fine, but on the production domain the API key must be a valid Web-app key (not a random string). Re-check REACT_APP_FIREBASE_API_KEY against Firebase Console → Project Settings → Web app config.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py at 1888 lines is very long — split into routers (auth/, payments/, mlm/, admin/, orders/) for maintainability.

_easebuzz_process_response fires MongoDB stock decrement without concurrency guards — two concurrent successful webhooks for the same order would race. Guard the paid-status transition with a conditional update: db.orders.update_one({id, payment_status: {$ne: 'paid'}}, ...) and use modified_count==1 as the mutex.

process_paid_joining trigger inside easebuzz webhook checks `any(i.get('is_hamper') for i in order.items)` — good — but the followup `.get('is_joining_paid')` on the user is called with only projection {'is_joining_paid':1} — the projection excludes _id by default in Motor? Actually _id is included; harmless.

mlm/re-entry: `new_ref_code = f"{new_user_code[-6:]}{uuid[:2]}"` gives 8-char code which collides with normal 8-char user_code prefixes over time. Consider a dedicated prefix (e.g. 'R' + user_code) to keep re-entry codes visually distinct in admin panels.
firebase_utils.get_firebase_app raises RuntimeError if creds file missing but there's no health check surfaces this at boot — a mis-mounted secret would only surface on first OTP verify call.
Front-end: pw toggle icon at Login uses inline SVG; would benefit from lucide-react Eye/EyeOff for consistency with rest of app.

Calculator computes sum from computeForward correctly but the label 'Total Reachable Income' should link back to plan-theme so a single-source-of-truth prevents drift (this is exactly the drift that produced today's bug).

rca of the issue: Calculator vs BusinessPlan total mismatch RCA: /app/frontend/src/lib/plan-theme.js defines INCOME_LEVELS with per=[1200,400,50,300,50,200,50,100]. Sum of per×6^L for L=1..8 = 7200+14400+10800+388800+388800+9331200+13996800+167961600 = 192,099,600 (₹19,20,99,600). But the same file exports TOTAL_POTENTIAL = 203699600 (₹20,36,99,600) — a hardcoded value that is 11,600,000 higher than the actual sum of the level table. Business-Plan.jsx renders TOTAL_POTENTIAL; Calculator.jsx recomputes from computeForward → gets the mathematically-correct 192,099,600. Fix: either correct TOTAL_POTENTIAL to 192099600 (and update TOTAL_POTENTIAL_WORDS to 'Nineteen Crore Twenty Lakh Ninety Nine Thousand Six Hundred'), OR correct one of the per-level rates so the sum equals 203,699,600 (needs +11,600,000; e.g. L2 at ₹722.22 or L6 at ₹448.68 — no clean integer solution suggests the constant is wrong, not the table). Recommended fix: change TOTAL_POTENTIAL to 192099600.
